findings.title: Map an admitted logical-prefix range instead of the whole native descriptor
findings.scenario: A valid Buffer::new(context,6.into(),BufferDefinition::map_read()) has SDK descriptor size6. Keeping native buffer unchanged and setting public logical size4 is admitted by logical<=allocated and whole u32 host admission. read::<u32> maps slice(..), length6, which native SDK rejects as UnalignedRangeSize. A0..4 mapping is valid on the same device and allocation. This is retained behavior, newly discovered within the owned logical/native relationship, not a new successful-path regression.
source_proof: wgpu-core device/resource.rs1001-1095 validates mapped-at-creation alignment only when true; HAL padding does not change SDK descriptor size.
wgpu-core resource.rs609-613 requires map range_size multiple of COPY_BUFFER_ALIGNMENT=4, then bounds checks permit0..4 for descriptor6.
d449 mapping.rs28-30 maps full descriptor, and read.rs45 obtains same whole view.
findings.minimum_connected_repair: Admit and retain one mapping extent covering logical bytes; round upward to native map-size alignment with checked arithmetic when trailing padding is needed; validate it fits the SDK descriptor; use that same retained range for map and get_mapped_range. Preserve logical3/physical4 byte-read success and honest errors when no aligned covering range fits. Keep zero bypass, typed-host preallocation, native policy and cleanup ownership unchanged.
findings.acceptance: Source must admit physical6/logical4 as mapping0..4; physical4/logical3 must still map4 and return3; impossible aligned covering range must return typed error before empty/out-of-bounds slice. Existing tests only, no new cases requested.
